problem: Two distinct vertices on the same side of one base cannot have the same respective distances to the base endpoints.

proof_idea.original: The source applies isosceles base-angle equality and geometric angle order to the competing triangle configurations.
proof_idea.analytic: Equal endpoint distances give equal projection dot products and equal determinant squares. The same-side positive determinant product fixes the sign. The two independent coordinate equations then force identical vertices.
